# Search ranks with BM25 in JavaScript (node:sqlite has no FTS5): an in-memory index per connection,…

Search ranks with BM25 in JavaScript (node:sqlite has no FTS5): an in-memory index per connection, rebuilt on change; every word must match, the last as a prefix; Turkish letters folded; Ask answers from the top 8 hits with [n] citations

FTS5 was the plan (task arama-fts5), but Node 22's node:sqlite is built without it ("no such module: fts5"). The data is small (about 9k records and 2.6k sections): the index builds in about 0.8 s and answers in about 20 ms after. Title words count twice; equal scores go newest first. MCP `search` returns records in rank order with a snippet when it adds to the title, plus up to five matching sections; a query the ranking cannot split falls back to the old text match. In VS Code, "Search and Ask" (ctrl/cmd+alt+k; Cmd+K is VS Code's chord prefix) updates as you type, this window's repos first; its first row asks the question with Sonnet through the user's Claude and opens the answer with its sources as a Markdown preview.
